# E0430: `when` inside a `when`

Holding one shared value while waiting for another could deadlock. Hold both in one `when`, as `when a, b { … }`.

- Rule: [`shared.locks`](../../reference/14-tasks.md#shared.locks)
- Reported at: the inner `when`, or the call of a function that has `locks`.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `analyses` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0430:8
use std.sync

type Account = { balance: i64 }

fn moved(a: sync.Shared<Account>, b: sync.Shared<Account>, n: i64) {
  when a {
    a.balance -= n
    when b { b.balance += n }
  }
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
use std.sync

type Account = { balance: i64 }

fn moved(a: sync.Shared<Account>, b: sync.Shared<Account>, n: i64) {
  when a, b {
    a.balance -= n
    b.balance += n
  }
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0430_when_inside_a_when.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0430_when_inside_a_when.lt):

```text
── `when` INSIDE A `when` ───────────── E0430_when_inside_a_when.lt:8:5  [E0430]

This `when` waits for its values while the `when` around it holds others, which
could deadlock:

  6 │   when a {
    │   ──────── this `when` holds its values for its whole block
  7 │     a.balance -= n
  8 │     when b { b.balance += n }
    │     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Holding one shared value while waiting for another could deadlock. Hold both in
one `when`, as `when a, b { … }`.
```
